long_biography.plain_text:
Kirchdoerffer founded Senstronic near Strasbourg in 1986 and built its expertise around industrial detection. An engineer and named inventor, he helped develop sensors and connectors designed for difficult environments, supplying automotive production lines before broadening into aerospace, rail and agricultural machinery. The business expanded internationally while retaining engineering and manufacturing in Alsace.

Preparing for retirement, Kirchdoerffer recruited Philippe Desnos to lead the company and arranged a management transition. A 2022 buyout brought Andera Partners in as majority shareholder and transferred operating leadership to Desnos. Kirchdoerffer has since registered Swiss companies for consulting, project management and investment-related work. His durable business identity remains the founder-engineer behind an industrial sensor manufacturer.

Public maritime data identifies Navy Storm Ltd as the yacht's registered owner, while a 2006 official deed shows Rémy Kirchdoerffer creating Navystorm S.A. for ship acquisition, chartering and management. The two similarly named entities have different displayed legal forms and are not treated as identical without a registry chain; the connection is corroborative rather than a claim of corporate continuity.

Sources use Remi, Remy, Rémi and Rémy. Current Swiss registry-derived records provide the full legal form Rémi Jean Kirchdoerffer, so the dossier proposes that canonical display and first-name spelling. Older French and Luxembourg records using Rémy remain valid historical orthography rather than a different person.

Current Swiss company records explicitly describe Kirchdoerffer as a French citizen resident in Switzerland, and the notarised Luxembourg record gives Strasbourg, France, and 19 June 1958. The existing Swiss nationality, Switzerland birth country and day 1 appear to conflate residence with nationality and birthplace; corrections are proposed. No evidence establishes Swiss dual nationality.

Kirchdoerffer retired from Senstronic and transferred leadership and majority control in 2022. His current Swiss entities have broad corporate purposes across consulting, projects, investment support, real estate and automotive work, but public records do not demonstrate realised activity or a dominant sector. Primary industry is therefore Unknown rather than inferred from purpose clauses.

The 2022 transaction establishes a founder exit and management succession, but reviewed sources do not disclose Kirchdoerffer's proceeds, retained stake, current net worth or ownership of the Swiss companies beyond his director status. No company, yacht or patent asset is equated with personal net worth.
